title: Pre-SOW Discovery & Scoping Questionnaire
lede: The companion instrument to the post-SOW readiness survey, fielded before signature. Its job is not readiness — it is scope accuracy. Every answer either sizes the SOW or becomes a written assumption that protects it, and every unanswered question is a change order waiting to happen.

questions.text: Full name
Job title and department
What is your role in this evaluation?
Have you been through a platform migration like this before?
questions.logic: A first-time migration team needs more hand-holding hours than an experienced one. This is an effort input, not a judgment, and it belongs in the estimate.

questions.text: Who else must be in the room before this can be signed?
What is driving this now?
What is the date that cannot move, and what happens if it does?
questions.logic: A hard date with a named consequence is a real date. A hard date with no consequence is a preference, and it should not drive a phase plan or a premium.

questions.text: What is wrong with what you have today, in the words you would use to your own executive?
Is an incumbent contract still running?
questions.logic: Overlap between an incumbent contract and a new platform is a budget conversation, not a technical one, but it reshapes the phase plan. Dual-running costs belong in the proposal, stated.

questions.text: Has a decision effectively been made, or is this a genuine evaluation?
options: Required to run a competitive process

questions.text: Current telephony platform and version
Current contact-centre platform, if separate from telephony
Employees in total: ____  ·  Employees who need a phone: ____  ·  Contact-centre agents: ____
How many physical sites?
Which of these are in use today and expected to survive the migration?
Who administers the current platform day to day?
questions.logic: "Nobody clearly owns it" is not a complaint — it is an estimate input. It means discovery will be archaeology, and the hours should say so.

questions.text: How well documented is the current configuration?
questions.logic: This is the single largest swing factor in discovery hours. Anything below "fully documented and current" means the estimate carries discovery as its own line item, not as an assumption.

questions.text: What has been tried before and did not work?
RingEX users expected: ____  ·  RingCX agent seats expected: ____  ·  Supervisor seats: ____
Is the agent count growing, flat or shrinking over the next 12 months?
Do agents work from one site, several, or from home?
Busiest-hour inbound calls: ____  ·  Daily inbound calls: ____  ·  Daily outbound calls: ____
questions.logic: Re-asked after signature as B2.3 against real reporting. The pre/post delta is the point — do not pre-fill it there.

questions.text: Where do the numbers in P3.4 come from?
questions.logic: The highest-leverage question in the instrument. A remembered number carried into a fixed-fee SOW is a margin problem discovered during build. Anything other than "exported from a reporting system" converts into a written assumption with a re-baseline clause.

questions.text: How many queues or routing destinations exist today?
questions.logic: Queue count drives RingCX gate and gate-group build hours more directly than agent count does.

questions.text: Will routing be rebuilt to match what exists today, or redesigned?
questions.logic: "Undecided" at signature is the most expensive answer on this page. If it cannot be resolved, the SOW prices lift-and-shift and names redesign as a separate engagement.

questions.text: How many IVR menus or auto-attendants are in scope?
Which systems must RingCentral connect to?
For the primary integration, what does "integrated" mean to you?
questions.logic: Each of these is a different amount of work and some are a packaged app rather than a build. "Not yet defined" is scoped as a discovery workshop, never as an integration.

questions.text: Is Microsoft Teams in use for calling today?
questions.logic: Teams calling in place changes the RingEX conversation from replacement to coexistence, and the two have different licence and routing shapes.

questions.text: How should user identity be managed?
options: Directory sync from Entra ID or Okta with SCIM
questions.logic: Where RingCX agents are not managed by RingEX identity, every joiner-mover-leaver is two pieces of work and offboarding has two places to fail. That is a design decision made here or an operational problem discovered later.

questions.text: Is single sign-on required at go-live?
Describe anything custom that touches telephony today — scripts, middleware, wallboards, dashboards, recording exports.
DIDs to port: ____  ·  Toll-free numbers: ____  ·  Carriers involved: ____
Do you have current CSRs or carrier bills for all numbers?
questions.logic: Porting timelines are gated entirely on documentation the customer supplies. Anything other than "yes, all" converts to a timeline assumption rather than a task.

questions.text: Ingress and edge requirements
Emergency-address complexity:
options: Dispatchable location per floor or room
questions.logic: RAY BAUM'S Act dispatchable-location-per-room is a distinct workstream with its own discovery, not a configuration checkbox. It belongs as a line item, and it is the finding most likely to appear in the first optimization review if it is skipped.

questions.text: Are any numbers bundled or contracted in a way that blocks porting?
Is business SMS or MMS in scope on any ported number?
questions.logic: SMS on a ported number requires A2P 10DLC brand and campaign registration, which is a lead-time item owned by the customer and gated on their legal entity details. It is never a day-one capability, and the SOW should say so.

questions.text: Is fax still in use, and must it survive?
options: Being retired as part of this project

questions.text: Anything unusual about the number estate — main lines, hunt groups, fax, alarm circuits, elevator lines, overhead paging.
Which capabilities do you want, and when?
questions.logic: Becomes the scope baseline that the post-SOW A6.8 is measured against. The delta between what they asked for here and what they believe they bought there is a measurable trust signal — and the only way to get it is to ask the same question twice, deliberately.

questions.text: For anything marked "need to understand it first," what is your question?
questions.logic: Feeds the demo agenda, and prevents a module being quoted into a SOW that the buyer never actually understood.

questions.text: Has anyone in your organization approved AI handling or analysing customer conversations?
questions.logic: AI governance is a common late-stage blocker and it kills the highest-margin modules. "Not raised yet" on a SOW carrying a RingCX AI agent or RingSense means those modules should be conditional or phase 2, not phase 1.

questions.text: Is call recording required, and for whom?
questions.logic: Recording scope sets the ceiling on everything downstream — quality management, RingSense coverage and dispute defence can only ever cover what was recorded.

questions.text: Is there a retention requirement on recordings or messages?
options: Yes, but the period is not defined
questions.logic: A stated retention period that exceeds the platform default is an Archiver conversation and a storage cost, both of which belong in the proposal rather than in a surprise.

questions.text: Which of these apply?
options: Frozen change window during part of the year
questions.logic: Each of these is a named multiplier in section 3. They are not disqualifiers; they are hours.

questions.text: How many languages must be supported in routing and prompts?
Will any part of the deployment be outside the country of the headquarters?
questions.logic: Numbering, emergency services and data residency are all country-specific. A multi-country deployment is several small projects, not one large one.

questions.text: Is there a maintenance or change-freeze window that constrains cutover?
How much of the migration can be phased, and how much must be a single cutover?
options: Fully phaseable by site or team
questions.logic: A forced single cutover changes the risk profile and the weekend-hours line in the estimate. It is a price input, not a preference.

questions.text: Is there an approved budget?
What is the approval path?
Target signature date
Target go-live date
Is professional services expected to be fixed fee or time and materials?
questions.logic: A fixed fee against an undocumented current state and a remembered call volume is the combination that produces a loss. If both are true, the assumptions in section 4 are the entire protection.

questions.text: What do you already know will be difficult?
Is there anything in the current environment that must not be touched?
Anything else that would change how we scope this?
